_comment: ARCHIVED - one round's opening template, kept as a worked example. The
instrument now uses templates/data_use_demo_intro_en.json, which says the
same things without naming a particular event: an opener that welcomes
somebody to a training they are not attending cannot be reused, and after
submission the wording can never be edited.
It replaced an earlier template that was approved under a *different*
WhatsApp Business Account, which is the lesson worth keeping: approval
attaches to the account, so a content SID that works for one sender fails
with error 63027 from another. Creating the template from the account that
will send it is what gets it approved under the right WABA.
Framed for UTILITY, not MARKETING. It names the training the participant is
already attending and states plainly what will happen, with no persuasion.
Every approved opening in this account that leads with an incentive or with
excitement landed in MARKETING, which carries per-user limits and worse
delivery. See .claude/skills/whatsapp-template/references/ipa-examples.md.
The quick-reply button matters mechanically, not just for tone: the flow's
intro widget is send-and-wait-for-reply, so tapping Start is what opens the
24-hour window and lets every later message be free-form.
'confidential' is a claim the pipeline actually keeps - encrypt_fields
encrypts name and phone before anything is stored.

twilio/quick-reply.body:
Hi {{1}}, welcome to the Research Staff Training 2026 in Jaipur.

During the WhatsApp session you will take part in a short survey - and you are also part of the example.

It takes about 3 minutes. Your answers are confidential and will only be used to illustrate WhatsApp data collection during the session.

Press Start when you are ready.
